# Kalpasūtra pilot — Jinacaritra: the Namokkāra and §§1–4. Drafted 2026-11-21 from Jacobi's text alone.
# One block per unit. "W reading | lemma — gloss ;; lemma — gloss" (a reading seen before may stand alone and reuses its entry);
# "--" marks a verse line break; L literal, I idiomatic, N note.

#U
W Namo | namo (Skt namas) — homage, salutation (indeclinable)
W arihaṃtāṇaṃ | arihaṃta (Skt arhat) — Arhat, a Jina: one who has conquered the passions and teaches while still in the body (gen. pl.)
W namo
W siddhāṇaṃ | siddha — Siddha, a soul that is perfected and freed from the body for ever (gen. pl.)
W namo
W āyariyāṇaṃ | āyariya (Skt ācārya) — Ācārya, a head of a monastic order (gen. pl.)
W namo
W uvajjhāyāṇaṃ | uvajjhāya (Skt upādhyāya) — Upādhyāya, a monk who teaches the scriptures (gen. pl.)
W namo
W loe | loa (Skt loka) — world (loc. sg. 'in the world')
W savva-sāhūṇaṃ | savva (Skt sarva) — all ;; sāhu (Skt sādhu) — holy man, monk (gen. pl.)
L: Homage to-the-Arhats, homage to-the-Siddhas, homage to-the-Ācāryas, homage to-the-Upādhyāyas, homage in-the-world to-all-the-sādhus.
I: Homage to the Arhats, homage to the Siddhas, homage to the Ācāryas, homage to the Upādhyāyas, homage to all the sādhus in the world.
N: The Namokkāra (Sanskrit Namaskāra), the salutation every Jain knows by heart, to the five supreme beings: Arhats, enlightened teachers still living in a body; Siddhas, liberated souls; Ācāryas, heads of the monastic orders; Upādhyāyas, teachers of scripture; and all monks. It names no person, only kinds of holiness. Grammar: namo takes the genitive (-āṇaṃ, Sanskrit -ānām), because Prakrit has lost the dative and uses the genitive in its place. Jacobi notes that manuscript M lacks this opening blessing.

#U
W eso | esa (Skt eṣa) — this (nom. sg. masc.)
W paṃca-namokkāro | paṃca (Skt pañca) — five ;; namokkāra (Skt namaskāra) — salutation (nom. sg.: 'the fivefold salutation')
W savva-pāva-ppaṇāsaṇo | savva — all ;; pāva (Skt pāpa) — evil, sin ;; ppaṇāsaṇa (Skt praṇāśana) — destroying (nom. sg.; pp doubled at the compound seam)
--
W maṃgalāṇaṃ | maṃgala (Skt maṅgala) — blessing, auspicious thing (gen. pl.)
W ca | ca — and
W savvesiṃ | savva — all (savvesiṃ: gen. pl., Skt sarveṣām)
W paḍhamaṃ | paḍhama (Skt prathama) — first (nom. sg. neut.)
W havai | ho / hava (Skt bhū) — to be, become (havai: pres. 3 sg., Skt bhavati)
W maṃgalaṃ | maṃgala — blessing (nom. sg.)
L: This five-salutation all-evil-destroying,
and of-blessings of-all first is blessing.
I: This fivefold salutation destroys all evil, and of all blessings it is the first blessing.
N: The verse that closes the Namokkāra in daily recitation. Here you can watch Prakrit sound changes at work: eso for Sanskrit eṣaḥ (-aḥ becomes -o), pāva for pāpa (a p between vowels softens to v), havai for bhavati (bh becomes h, and the t between vowels drops out). That last change, the loss of a consonant between vowels, is everywhere in this text.

#U 1
W Teṇaṃ | ta (Skt tad) — that (teṇaṃ: instr. sg., Skt tena)
W kāleṇaṃ | kāla — time, age (instr. sg.)
W teṇaṃ
W samaeṇaṃ | samaa (Skt samaya) — moment, occasion (instr. sg.)
W samaṇe | samaṇa (Skt śramaṇa) — ascetic, wandering renouncer (nom. sg.)
W bhagavaṃ | bhagavaṃta (Skt bhagavat) — the Blessed One, the Lord (nom. sg.)
W Mahāvīre | Mahāvīra — Mahāvīra, 'great hero', the twenty-fourth Jina (nom. sg.)
W paṃca-hatth’uttare | paṃca — five ;; hatth’uttara (Skt hastottarā) — Hastottarā, the lunar mansion after Hasta, i.e. Uttaraphalgunī (nom. sg. masc., 'having five events in Hastottarā')
W hotthā | ho (Skt bhū) — to be (hotthā: old past tense, 'was')
L: In-that time, in-that occasion the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra five-Hastottarā was;
I: In that age, at that time, the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, had five events under the asterism Hastottarā:
N: Teṇaṃ kāleṇaṃ teṇaṃ samaeṇaṃ opens narrative after narrative in the Jain scriptures, as 'once upon a time' does in English. The instrumental (-eṇaṃ) is used for time. Note the nominative in -e (samaṇe, Mahāvīre) where Sanskrit has -aḥ: this is the eastern ending typical of Ardhamāgadhī, and you'll see it constantly. Hastottarā, 'the one after Hasta', is one of the 27 lunar mansions; events are dated by the mansion the moon stands in.

#U
W taṃ | ta — that (nom./acc. sg. neut.)
W jahā | jahā (Skt yathā) — as, namely
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ | hatth’uttara — the lunar mansion Hastottarā (instr. pl.: 'with Hastottarā', i.e. when the moon was in it)
W cue | cua (Skt cyuta) — fallen, descended from heaven (nom. sg.)
W caittā | cay / cu (Skt cyu) — to fall, descend (caittā: gerund, 'having descended')
W gabbhaṃ | gabbha (Skt garbha) — womb; embryo (acc. sg.)
W vakkaṃte | vakkaṃta (Skt avakrānta) — entered, descended into (nom. sg.)
L: that as-follows: with-Hastottarā fell, having-fallen womb entered,
I: namely, under Hastottarā he descended from heaven, and having descended he entered a womb;
N: Taṃ jahā (Sanskrit tad yathā) introduces a list. Cue, 'fallen', is the regular word for a god's soul leaving heaven when its life there ends. The gerund in -ittā (caittā, 'having fallen') is the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit -tvā; it strings actions together. The asterism is plural in form, hence the instrumental plural hatth’uttarāhiṃ.

#U
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ
W gabbhāo | gabbha — womb (abl. sg., Skt garbhāt)
W gabbhaṃ
W sāharie | sāharia (Skt saṃhṛta) — carried over, transferred (nom. sg.)
L: with-Hastottarā from-womb to-womb was-transferred,
I: under Hastottarā he was carried from one womb to another;
N: The second event: the transfer of the embryo, which the text tells at length later. In the Śvetāmbara account the god Śakra has the embryo moved from the brahmin woman Devānandā to the warrior-class queen Triśalā, since a Jina is born into a warrior family. The Digambaras reject the story. Ablative in -āo, Sanskrit -āt.

#U
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ
W jāe | jāa (Skt jāta) — born (nom. sg.)
L: with-Hastottarā was-born,
I: under Hastottarā he was born;
N: Jāe is Sanskrit jātaḥ: the t between vowels drops out and -aḥ becomes -e. Keep both changes in mind and many words in this text will become recognisable.

#U
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ
W muṃḍe | muṃḍa (Skt muṇḍa) — shaven (nom. sg.)
W bhavittā | ho (Skt bhū) — to be, become (bhavittā: gerund, 'having become')
W agārāo | agāra (Skt agāra) — house, home (abl. sg.)
W aṇagāriyaṃ | aṇagāriya (Skt anagāritā) — houselessness, the life of a wandering monk (acc. sg.)
W pavvaie | pavvaia (Skt pravrajita) — gone forth, become a monk (nom. sg.)
L: with-Hastottarā shaven having-become, from-home into-homelessness went-forth,
I: under Hastottarā he had his head shaved and went forth from home into homelessness;
N: The third event, his renunciation. Muṃḍa bhavittā, 'having become shaven', refers to the removal of the hair at initiation. Agārāo aṇagāriyaṃ pavvaie, 'went forth from the house into houselessness', is the standard phrase for becoming a monk; the same idiom appears in Buddhist texts.

#U
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ
W aṇaṃte | aṇaṃta (Skt ananta) — endless, infinite (nom. sg. neut.)
W aṇuttare | aṇuttara (Skt anuttara) — unsurpassed (nom. sg. neut.)
W nivvāghāe | nivvāghāa (Skt nirvyāghāta) — unobstructed (nom. sg. neut.)
W nirāvaraṇe | nirāvaraṇa — without a veil, unveiled (nom. sg. neut.)
W kasiṇe | kasiṇa (Skt kṛtsna) — whole, entire (nom. sg. neut.)
W paḍipunne | paḍipunna (Skt paripūrṇa) — full, complete (nom. sg. neut.)
W kevala-vara-nāṇa-daṃsaṇe | kevala — sole, absolute; kevala-nāṇa, omniscience ;; vara — supreme ;; nāṇa (Skt jñāna) — knowledge ;; daṃsaṇa (Skt darśana) — perception, intuition (nom. sg. neut.)
W samuppanne | samuppanna (Skt samutpanna) — arisen (nom. sg. neut.)
L: with-Hastottarā endless, unsurpassed, unobstructed, unveiled, whole, complete, the-kevala-supreme-knowledge-and-perception arose;
I: under Hastottarā there arose in him kevala, the supreme knowledge and perception: infinite, unsurpassed, unobstructed, unveiled, whole and complete;
N: The fourth event, his enlightenment. Kevala-nāṇa, knowledge that is 'sole' or 'absolute', is omniscience: the soul's own knowing, with nothing left of the karma that covers it (nirāvaraṇa, 'unveiled', names the absence of those covering karmas). Jain doctrine pairs knowledge (nāṇa) with perception (daṃsaṇa) as the soul's two capacities. In Ardhamāgadhī the neuter nominative also ends in -e, so here the subject is a neuter noun.

#U
W sāiṇā | sāi (Skt svāti) — Svāti, a lunar mansion, two after Hasta (instr. sg.)
W parinivvue | parinivvua (Skt parinirvṛta) — completely extinguished, gone to final liberation (nom. sg.)
W bhayavaṃ | bhayavaṃta — the Blessed One (nom. sg.; the same word as bhagavaṃ)
L: with-Svāti attained-final-nirvāṇa the-Blessed.
I: Under Svāti the Blessed One reached final liberation.
N: The fifth event breaks the pattern: Mahāvīra's death and liberation fall under a different lunar mansion, Svāti. Parinivvue, 'wholly extinguished', is the Prakrit form of parinirvṛta. Bhayavaṃ is bhagavaṃ with its g softened to a y sound between vowels; Jacobi keeps both spellings as the manuscripts have them.

#U 2
W teṇaṃ
W kāleṇaṃ
W teṇaṃ
W samaeṇaṃ
W samaṇe
W bhagavaṃ
W Mahāvīre
L: In-that time, in-that occasion the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra,
I: In that age, at that time, the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One,
N: The opening formula again, and the subject of §2 — which has to wait through a very long string of datings and descriptions for its verb, vakkaṃte, 'descended', at the very end of the section. Jain canonical prose likes to pile up phrases before a single finite verb; read on, holding the subject in mind.

#U
W je | ja (Skt yad) — which, who (nom. sg. masc.)
W se | ta — that, he (se: nom. sg. masc., Skt saḥ)
W gimhāṇaṃ | gimha (Skt grīṣma) — the hot season (gen. pl.)
W cautthe | cauttha (Skt caturtha) — fourth (loc. sg.)
W māse | māsa — month (loc. sg.)
W aṭṭhame | aṭṭhama (Skt aṣṭama) — eighth (loc. sg.)
W pakkhe | pakkha (Skt pakṣa) — fortnight, half of a lunar month (loc. sg.)
W āsāḍha-suddhe | āsāḍha (Skt āṣāḍha) — the month Āṣāḍha (June–July) ;; suddha (Skt śuddha) — bright, i.e. the waxing half (loc. sg.)
L: which that of-the-hot-season in-the-fourth month, in-the-eighth fortnight, in-Āṣāḍha-bright,
I: in the fourth month of the hot season, the eighth fortnight, the bright half of Āṣāḍha,
N: Je se, 'which that', is a stock way of introducing a date, picked up by tassa ṇaṃ in the next unit. The hot season has four months, so its fourth month, Āṣāḍha, holds its eighth fortnight; suddha, 'bright', is the half of the month when the moon waxes.

#U
W tassa | ta — that (tassa: gen. sg., Skt tasya)
W ṇaṃ | ṇaṃ — an emphatic particle with no English equivalent
W āsāḍha-suddhassa | āsāḍha — Āṣāḍha ;; suddha — bright half (gen. sg.)
W chaṭṭhī-pakkheṇaṃ | chaṭṭhī (Skt ṣaṣṭhī) — the sixth (day) ;; pakkha — fortnight (instr. sg.: 'on the sixth day of the fortnight')
W mahāvijaya-pupph’uttara-pavara-puṃḍarīyāo | mahāvijaya — 'great victory' ;; pupph’uttara (Skt puṣpottara) — Puṣpottara, the heavenly palace Mahāvīra came from ;; pavara (Skt pravara) — excellent ;; puṃḍarīya (Skt puṇḍarīka) — white lotus; the finest of its kind (abl. sg.)
W mahāvimāṇāo | mahā — great ;; vimāṇa (Skt vimāna) — heavenly palace, celestial dwelling of the gods (abl. sg.)
W vīsaṃ-sāgarovama-ṭṭhitīyāo | vīsaṃ (Skt viṃśati) — twenty ;; sāgarovama (Skt sāgaropama) — an 'ocean-measure', an immense unit of time ;; ṭṭhitīya (Skt sthitika) — having a duration of (abl. sg.)
L: of-that, ṇaṃ, Āṣāḍha-bright on-the-sixth-day, from-the-great-victory-Puṣpottara-excellent-lotus great-heavenly-palace twenty-ocean-measures-lasting,
I: on its sixth day, from Puṣpottara, the great heavenly palace of great victory, the finest lotus of them all, where life lasts twenty ocean-measures,
N: Ṇaṃ is a small emphatic particle that Ardhamāgadhī prose sprinkles everywhere; it adds nothing translatable, so read past it. A sāgarovama, 'ocean-measure', is a period of time beyond counting; Jain cosmology measures the lives of the gods in them. The long compound is a list of epithets of the palace in the ablative (-āo, 'from'); the -ṭṭh- doubles at the compound seam.

#U
W (āu-kkhaeṇaṃ | āu (Skt āyus) — lifespan ;; kkhaa (Skt kṣaya) — ending, exhaustion (instr. sg.)
W bhava-kkhaeṇaṃ | bhava — existence, a particular birth ;; kkhaa — ending (instr. sg.)
W ṭhii-kkhaeṇaṃ) | ṭhii (Skt sthiti) — stay, duration of residence ;; kkhaa — ending (instr. sg.)
W aṇaṃtaraṃ | aṇaṃtara (Skt anantara) — without interval; immediately (adverb)
W cayaṃ | caya (Skt cyava) — fall, descent (acc. sg.)
W caittā
L: (by-life-ending, by-existence-ending, by-stay-ending) immediately descent having-descended
I: (when his lifespan, his existence as a god and his stay there had run out,) he descended straight away,
N: Jacobi prints the three phrases in round brackets because manuscript A lacks them; one commentary marks them as found only in some copies. Cayaṃ caittā, 'having fallen a fall', pairs a verb with its own noun for emphasis. The god's soul descends the instant its heavenly life is used up: there is no interval (aṇaṃtaraṃ) between one existence and the next.

#U
W ih’ eva | iha — here ;; eva — just, indeed (ih’ eva: 'right here')
W Jaṃbuddīve | Jaṃbuddīva (Skt jambūdvīpa) — Jambūdvīpa, 'rose-apple continent', the central continent of the world (loc. sg.)
W dīve | dīva (Skt dvīpa) — continent, island (loc. sg.)
W Bhārahe | Bhāraha (Skt bhārata) — Bhārata, the southern region of Jambūdvīpa: India (loc. sg.)
W vāse | vāsa (Skt varṣa) — region, land (loc. sg.)
W imīse | ima (Skt idam) — this (imīse: loc. sg. fem.)
W osappiṇīe | osappiṇī (Skt avasarpiṇī) — the descending half of the cycle of time (loc. sg.)
L: right-here in-the-Jambū continent, in-the-Bhārata land, in-this descending-age,
I: here in the continent of Jambūdvīpa, in the land of Bhārata, in this present descending age,
N: Jain cosmography places our world on Jambūdvīpa, a ring-shaped central continent; Bhārata is its southern land, India. Time turns in endless cycles, each half divided into six eras; in the descending half (osappiṇī, Sanskrit avasarpiṇī) everything slowly declines. The locatives in -e and the feminine locative in -īe set the scene.

#U
W susama-susamāe | susamā (Skt suṣamā) — happiness; doubled, susama-susamā, 'happy-happy', the first and best era (loc. sg.)
W samāe | samā — era, period (loc. sg.)
W viikkaṃtāe | viikkaṃta (Skt vyatikrānta) — passed by, gone (loc. sg. fem.)
W susamāe | susamā — the 'happy' era (loc. sg.)
W samāe
W viikkaṃtāe
W susama-dussamāe | susamā — happiness ;; dussamā (Skt duḥṣamā) — misery; susama-dussamā, the 'happy-unhappy' era (loc. sg.)
W samāe
W viikkaṃtāe
W dussama-susamāe | dussamā — misery ;; susamā — happiness; dussama-susamā, the 'unhappy-happy' era (loc. sg.)
W samāe
W bahu-viikkaṃtāe | bahu — much ;; viikkaṃta — passed (loc. sg. fem.: 'mostly passed')
W [sāgarovama-koḍākoḍīe | sāgarovama — ocean-measure ;; koḍākoḍī (Skt koṭikoṭi) — a crore of crores, a hundred million million (loc. sg.)
W bāyālīsāe | bāyālīsā (Skt dvācatvāriṃśat) — forty-two (instr. sg.)
W vāsa-sahassehiṃ | vāsa (Skt varṣa) — year ;; sahassa (Skt sahasra) — thousand (instr. pl.)
W ūṇiyāe] | ūṇiyā (Skt ūnikā) — lacking, less (loc. sg. fem.)
L: the-happy-happy era having-passed, the-happy era having-passed, the-happy-unhappy era having-passed, the-unhappy-happy era much-having-passed [a-crore-of-crores-of-ocean-measures by-forty-two year-thousands lacking]
I: when the 'very happy' era had passed, and the 'happy' era, and the 'happy-unhappy' era, and most of the 'unhappy-happy' era had gone by [an era of a hundred million million ocean-measures, less forty-two thousand years],
N: A chain of locative absolutes, 'the era having passed': four of the six eras of the descending half, named by their balance of happiness (susamā) and misery (dussamā). The fourth era, in which all twenty-four Jinas of this cycle live, is the one now nearly over. Jacobi puts the bracketed phrase in square brackets because manuscripts A and C lack it and B has it only in the margin.

#U
W paṃca-hattarīe | paṃca — five ;; hattarī (Skt saptati) — seventy; paṃca-hattarī, seventy-five (instr. sg.)
W vāsehiṃ | vāsa — year (instr. pl.)
W addha-navamehi | addha (Skt ardha) — half ;; navama — ninth; addha-navama, 'with the ninth half', eight and a half (instr. pl.)
W ya | ya (Skt ca) — and
W māsehiṃ | māsa — month (instr. pl.)
W sesehiṃ | sesa (Skt śeṣa) — remaining (instr. pl.)
L: seventy-five years and eight-and-a-half months remaining,
I: with seventy-five years and eight and a half months of it still to run,
N: Addha-navama, 'half-ninth', means eight and a half: the ninth month counts only by half. The same idiom exists in Sanskrit and Pali. Ya is ca, 'and', with its c dropped between vowels and a y sound bridging the gap. An instrumental absolute: 'with seventy-five years remaining'.

#U
W ekka-vīsāe | ekka (Skt eka) — one ;; vīsā (Skt viṃśati) — twenty; ekka-vīsā, twenty-one (instr. sg.)
W titthayarehiṃ | titthayara (Skt tīrthaṃkara) — Tīrthaṅkara, 'ford-maker', a Jina (instr. pl.)
W Ikkhāga-kula-samuppannehiṃ | Ikkhāga (Skt ikṣvāku) — the Ikṣvāku dynasty ;; kula — family ;; samuppanna — born, arisen (instr. pl.)
W Kāsava-gottehiṃ | Kāsava (Skt kāśyapa) — Kāśyapa ;; gotta (Skt gotra) — clan, lineage (instr. pl.)
W dohi | do (Skt dvi) — two (instr.)
W ya
W Harivaṃsa-kula-samuppannehiṃ | Harivaṃsa (Skt harivaṃśa) — the Harivaṃśa dynasty ;; kula — family ;; samuppanna — born (instr. pl.)
W Goyama-sagottehiṃ | Goyama (Skt gautama) — Gautama ;; sagotta — of the clan (instr. pl.)
W tevīsāe | tevīsā (Skt trayoviṃśati) — twenty-three (instr. sg.)
W titthayarehiṃ
W viikkaṃtehiṃ | viikkaṃta — passed, gone (instr. pl.)
L: twenty-one Tīrthaṅkaras Ikṣvāku-family-born of-Kāśyapa-clan, and two Harivaṃśa-family-born of-Gautama-clan, twenty-three Tīrthaṅkaras having-passed,
I: after twenty-three Tīrthaṅkaras had come and gone, twenty-one of them born in the Ikṣvāku family, of the Kāśyapa clan, and two born in the Harivaṃśa family, of the Gautama clan,
N: Titthayara, 'ford-maker', is the Jain title for a Jina: one who makes a crossing (tittha) over the ocean of rebirth for others to follow. Mahāvīra is the twenty-fourth and last of this cycle. The two of the Harivaṃśa family are Munisuvrata and Nemi, the twentieth and twenty-second. Another instrumental absolute, closing the long dating.

#U
W samaṇe
W bhagavaṃ
W Mahāvīre
W carime | carima (Skt carama) — last (nom. sg.)
W titthayare | titthayara — Tīrthaṅkara (nom. sg.)
W puvva-titthayara-niddiṭṭhe | puvva (Skt pūrva) — earlier, former ;; titthayara — Tīrthaṅkara ;; niddiṭṭha (Skt nirdiṣṭa) — pointed out, foretold (nom. sg.)
L: the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra, the-last Tīrthaṅkara, by-former-Tīrthaṅkaras-foretold,
I: the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, the last Tīrthaṅkara, whose coming the earlier Tīrthaṅkaras had foretold,
N: After the dating the subject is repeated, so the reader can find the thread again. Carima, 'last', is a title as much as a description: with him the line of twenty-four is complete.

#U
W māhaṇa-Kuṃḍaggāme | māhaṇa (Skt brāhmaṇa) — brahmin ;; Kuṃḍaggāma (Skt kuṇḍagrāma) — Kuṇḍagrāma, a town near Vaiśālī (loc. sg.: 'in Brahmin Kuṇḍagrāma')
W nayare | nayara (Skt nagara) — town (loc. sg.)
W Usabhadattassa | Usabhadatta (Skt ṛṣabhadatta) — Ṛṣabhadatta, Devānandā's husband (gen. sg.)
W māhaṇassa | māhaṇa — brahmin (gen. sg.)
W Koḍāla-sagottassa | Koḍāla — the Koḍāla clan ;; sagotta — belonging to the clan (gen. sg.)
W bhāriyāe | bhāriyā (Skt bhāryā) — wife (gen. sg.)
W Devāṇaṃdāe | Devāṇaṃdā (Skt devānandā) — Devānandā, Mahāvīra's first mother (gen. sg.)
W māhaṇīe | māhaṇī (Skt brāhmaṇī) — brahmin woman (gen. sg.)
W Jālaṃdhara-sagottāe | Jālaṃdhara — the Jālandhara clan ;; sagotta — belonging to the clan (gen. sg. fem.)
L: in-the-brahmin-Kuṇḍagrāma town, of-Ṛṣabhadatta the-brahmin of-the-Koḍāla-clan, of-the-wife Devānandā the-brahmin-woman of-the-Jālandhara-clan,
I: in the town of Brahmin Kuṇḍagrāma, into the womb of Devānandā, brahmin wife of the brahmin Ṛṣabhadatta, he of the Koḍāla clan and she of the Jālandhara clan,
N: Kuṇḍagrāma had a brahmin quarter and a warrior quarter; the embryo will later be moved from one to the other. Māhaṇa is the Ardhamāgadhī form of brāhmaṇa. The feminine genitive ends in -āe or -īe, the same as the locative: these genitives depend on kucchiṃsi, 'in the womb', which comes two units later.

#U
W puvva-rattāvaratta-kāla-samayaṃsi | puvva-ratta (Skt pūrva-rātra) — the first part of the night ;; avaratta (Skt apara-rātra) — the latter part of the night ;; kāla-samaya — time, moment (loc. sg.: 'at the moment between the two halves of the night', midnight)
W hatth’uttarāhiṃ
W nakkhatteṇaṃ | nakkhatta (Skt nakṣatra) — lunar mansion, asterism (instr. sg.)
W jogam uvāgaeṇaṃ | joga (Skt yoga) — conjunction, union (acc. sg.; m kept before a vowel) ;; uvāgaa (Skt upāgata) — come to (instr. sg.)
L: at-the-first-night-latter-night-time-moment, with-Hastottarā the-asterism conjunction having-come-to,
I: at midnight, when the moon had come into conjunction with the asterism Hastottarā,
N: Puvva-ratta-avaratta, 'the first night and the later night', is the moment where they meet: midnight. The locative in -aṃsi (Sanskrit -asmin) is distinctive of Ardhamāgadhī; you'll see it constantly. Jogam uvāgaeṇaṃ, 'having come into union', is said of the asterism meeting the moon; the m of jogam is kept before the following vowel and the two words are written together in Devanagari.

#U
W āhāra-vakkaṃtīe | āhāra — food, nourishment ;; vakkaṃti (Skt avakrānti) — descent, entry (instr. sg.)
W bhava-vakkaṃtīe | bhava — existence, birth ;; vakkaṃti — descent (instr. sg.)
W sarīra-vakkaṃtīe | sarīra (Skt śarīra) — body ;; vakkaṃti — descent (instr. sg.)
W kucchiṃsi | kucchi (Skt kukṣi) — belly, womb (loc. sg.)
W gabbhattāe | gabbhattā (Skt garbhatā) — the state of an embryo (instr./dat. sg.: 'as an embryo')
W vakkaṃte
L: with-food-descent, with-existence-descent, with-body-descent, in-the-womb as-embryo descended.
I: descended into her womb as an embryo, taking on a new nourishment, a new existence and a new body.
N: Here at last is the verb of §2, vakkaṃte, 'descended'. The three vakkaṃti phrases name what changes when a soul passes from heaven into a womb: what feeds it, what kind of existence it has, and what body it wears. Gabbhattāe, 'into embryo-hood', uses the abstract suffix -ttā (Sanskrit -tā).

#U 3
W samaṇe
W bhagavaṃ
W Mahāvīre
W tiṇ-ṇāṇovagae | ti (Skt tri) — three ;; ṇāṇa — knowledge ;; uvagaa (Skt upagata) — possessed of (nom. sg.: 'possessed of three kinds of knowledge')
W āvi | āvi (Skt api) — also, even
W hotthā
L: The-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra, three-knowledge-possessed even was.
I: The ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, had three kinds of knowledge.
N: Jain teaching counts five kinds of knowledge: through the senses, through scripture, clairvoyance, knowledge of others' minds, and omniscience. A future Jina is born with the first three; the fourth comes when he becomes a monk, and the fifth, omniscience, at his enlightenment. Ṇāṇa + uvagaa contract to -ṇovagae, the o that Jacobi marks with a dot.

#U
W ‘caissāmi’ | cay / cu — to fall, descend (caissāmi: fut. 1 sg., 'I shall descend')
W tti | tti (Skt iti) — thus (closes a quotation)
W jāṇai | jāṇ (Skt jñā) — to know (jāṇai: pres. 3 sg.)
W cayamāṇe | cayamāṇa — descending (pres. participle, nom. sg.)
W na | na — not
W jāṇai
W ‘cue | cua — fallen, descended
W ’mi’ | ’mi (Skt asmi) — I am (amhi/ammi with the a elided)
W tti
W jāṇai.
L: ‘I-shall-descend’ thus he-knows, descending not he-knows, ‘descended I-am’ thus he-knows.
I: He knew, ‘I am going to descend’; while he was descending he did not know it; he knew, ‘I have descended.’
N: The present jāṇai, 'knows', tells a past event, as English can say 'he knows' in a story. Tti (Sanskrit iti) marks the words in quotation marks as his thought. Jain commentators explain the middle clause as follows: the descent takes a single instant, the smallest unit of time, too brief for any knowledge short of omniscience to grasp.

#U
W jaṃ | ja — which (jaṃ: acc. sg. fem.)
W rayaṇiṃ | rayaṇī (Skt rajanī) — night (acc. sg.)
W ca | ca — and
W ṇaṃ
W samaṇe
W bhagavaṃ
W Mahāvīre
W Devāṇaṃdāe
W māhaṇīe
W Jālaṃdhara-sagottāe
W kucchiṃsi
W gabbhattāe
W vakkaṃte
L: On-which night ṇaṃ the-ascetic, the-Blessed, Mahāvīra into-the-womb of-Devānandā the-brahmin-woman of-the-Jālandhara-clan as-embryo descended,
I: On the night when the ascetic Mahāvīra, the Blessed One, descended as an embryo into the womb of Devānandā, the brahmin woman of the Jālandhara clan,
N: Jaṃ rayaṇiṃ ... taṃ rayaṇiṃ, 'on which night ... on that night': a relative clause answered by a correlative, the usual Indic way of building such a sentence. The accusative marks a stretch of time. The whole clause repeats the words of §2 almost exactly; repetition of this kind is part of the text's style.

#U
W taṃ
W rayaṇiṃ
W ca
W ṇaṃ
W sā | ta — that, she (sā: nom. sg. fem.)
W Devāṇaṃdā | Devāṇaṃdā — Devānandā (nom. sg.)
W māhaṇī | māhaṇī — brahmin woman (nom. sg.)
W sayaṇijjaṃsi | sayaṇijja (Skt śayanīya) — bed, couch (loc. sg.)
W sutta-jāgarā | sutta (Skt supta) — asleep ;; jāgara — awake (nom. sg. fem.: 'between sleep and waking')
W ohīramāṇī | ohīr — to doze, nod off (ohīramāṇī: pres. participle, nom. sg. fem.; the word is rare and its origin uncertain)
L: on-that night ṇaṃ she Devānandā the-brahmin-woman on-the-bed asleep-awake dozing
I: that night the brahmin woman Devānandā, lying on her bed between sleep and waking, drowsing,
N: Sutta-jāgarā, 'asleep-awake', is the half-conscious state in which, in Indian tradition, prophetic dreams come. Ohīramāṇī, 'dozing', is a rare word whose origin is uncertain; its sense is clear from the context and from the commentaries. Another locative in -aṃsi: sayaṇijjaṃsi, 'on the bed'.

#U
W ime | ima — this (ime: acc. pl. masc.)
W eyārūve | eyārūva (Skt etad-rūpa) — of such a kind (acc. pl.)
W orāle | orāla (Skt udāra) — grand, splendid (acc. pl.)
W kallāṇe | kallāṇa (Skt kalyāṇa) — fortunate, lovely (acc. pl.)
W sive | siva (Skt śiva) — propitious (acc. pl.)
W dhanne | dhanna (Skt dhanya) — bringing wealth, prosperous (acc. pl.)
W maṃgalle | maṃgalla (Skt māṅgalya) — auspicious, blessed (acc. pl.)
W sassirīe | sassirīa (Skt saśrīka) — glorious (acc. pl.)
W coddasa | coddasa (Skt caturdaśa) — fourteen
W mahāsumiṇe | mahā — great ;; sumiṇa (Skt svapna) — dream (acc. pl.)
W pāsittā | pās (Skt paś) — to see (pāsittā: gerund, 'having seen')
W ṇaṃ
W paḍibuddhā | paḍibuddha (Skt pratibuddha) — awakened (nom. sg. fem.)
L: these such-formed grand, fortunate, propitious, prosperous, blessed, glorious fourteen great-dreams having-seen ṇaṃ awoke.
I: saw these fourteen great dreams, splendid, fortunate, propitious, prosperous, blessed and glorious, and awoke.
N: The mother of every Tīrthaṅkara sees fourteen great dreams on the night of his conception (Digambaras count sixteen). The masculine accusative plural ends in -e in Ardhamāgadhī, the same as the nominative singular, so the endings alone will not tell you which you have: the verb pāsittā, 'having seen', settles it. Sumiṇa is Sanskrit svapna, with a vowel inserted to break up the consonant cluster.

#U 4
W taṃ
W jahā
L: That as-follows,
I: They were these:
N: Taṃ jahā again introduces a list. What follows is a verse, the traditional memory-verse naming the fourteen dreams in order.

#U
W gaya | gaya (Skt gaja) — elephant
W vasaha | vasaha (Skt vṛṣabha) — bull
W sīha | sīha (Skt siṃha) — lion
W abhiseya | abhiseya (Skt abhiṣeka) — anointing; here the anointing of the goddess Śrī
--
W dāma | dāma (Skt dāman) — garland
W sasi | sasi (Skt śaśin) — the moon
W diṇayaraṃ | diṇayara (Skt dinakara) — 'day-maker', the sun (acc. sg.)
W jhayaṃ | jhaya (Skt dhvaja) — banner (acc. sg.)
W kuṃbhaṃ | kuṃbha (Skt kumbha) — jar, pitcher (acc. sg.)
--
W paumasara | pauma (Skt padma) — lotus ;; sara (Skt saras) — lake: 'lotus lake'
W sāgara | sāgara — ocean
W vimāṇa- | vimāṇa — heavenly palace
--
W bhavaṇa | bhavaṇa (Skt bhavana) — dwelling, palace (vimāṇa-bhavaṇa: a heavenly palace, or the palace of the gods below the earth)
W rayaṇ’-uccaya | rayaṇa (Skt ratna) — jewel ;; uccaya — heap: 'heap of jewels'
W sihiṃ | sihi (Skt śikhin) — fire, flame (acc. sg.)
W ca. | ca — and
L: elephant, bull, lion, anointing,
garland, moon, sun, banner, jar,
lotus-lake, ocean, palace-
dwelling, jewel-heap and flame.
I: An elephant, a bull, a lion, the anointing of the goddess Śrī, a garland, the moon, the sun, a banner, a jar, a lotus lake, the ocean, a heavenly palace, a heap of jewels and a flame.
N: The fourteen dreams in their canonical order, in the old āryā metre, which counts syllable lengths rather than syllables. Most items are bare stems with no ending, as in a list; a few take the accusative (diṇayaraṃ, jhayaṃ, kuṃbhaṃ, sihiṃ), the dreams being what she saw. Vimāṇa-bhavaṇa is split across the line: the tradition explains that a mother whose son comes down from heaven sees a heavenly palace (vimāṇa), and one whose son comes up from below sees a palace of the underworld gods (bhavaṇa).
